newsitem.title: UK: Emap board rift weighs heavily on shares.
newsitem.headline: Emap board rift weighs heavily on shares.

text.p: Shares in media group Emap Plc sunk on Thursday amid press speculation of a long-standing dispute among its key executives and as investors awaited feedback from an ongoing board meeting.
The shares fell 29-1/2p to 715p as nervous investors feared divisions ran much deeper than had previously been thought.

"Before today's front-page article in the FT (Financial Times)people had thought the management problems were just among the non-executives," said one leading media analyst who declined to be named. "Now it seems that it has spread to the chief executive and managing director and one of them might leave."

The FT said today that the board of Emap was "riven by dispute" and has been for years. But the report added that relations between chief executive Robin Miller and group managing director David Arculus are also "strained".
Analysts said that much of the group's past success was due to its strong management team, but they were now expecting one of the two executives to be forced to leave.
Emap's board met last night and the ongoing meeting is expected to wind up soon.
The company declined to comment on today's report in the FT or on what was being discussed at the meeting.
Emap's board meeting also follows reports of a board split over the future of chairman Sir John Hoskyns but a spokesman for the company denied today that the chairman's position was under review.
"There is no question of the chairman being removed," the spokesman said.
